title: Birthplace and boyhood neighborhoods in New Orleans
summary: Born on Calliope Street, he moved to Drive Street in the Garden District and later downtown to Padilla Street.

blocks.x: There's a whole lot of things I want to ask you about. Where were you born exactly? I was born here in New Orleans. What part of town? Do you know? Did they tell you?
I was born on Caliope, between Rides and Barone. My native home. This is my native home. I left here. I left here. Went to California. But no, you're jumping ahead too far.
And I hate to interrupt you, but I want to get that address business straight. Did you grow up there on Caliope? I grew up there.

Caliope was right on her own as a boy. Twenty-what age? Such ages as, I might say, well, I lived between Caliope and, oh, a boy twenty-seven, twenty-eight years of age. One hundred and a half years. Where did you move to from there? I moved up on Drive between Second and Third in the same neighborhood. I moved from Drive between Howard Avenue and Caliope to Drive between Second and Third in what we called the Garden District at that time. At that time, of course, the Garden District. All this was called the Garden District at that time.
What do you call it now?
Well, it's still called the Garden District. And, uh... A little further up to this. It's called the Jefferson, like they do now.
And then after you moved away from there, where did you move to?

After I moved away from there, I moved down on, I moved downtown then. I moved down on Padilla Street. I moved down on Padilla Street, Franklin and Liberty. I moved down on Padilla Street, Franklin and Liberty. I'm going to tell you about the school.
